labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

The bounded Desktop root-boundary recovery merged in #52704 is no longer present on current `main`.

The existing message-local `MessageRenderBoundary` handles many assistant-ui index races, but production reports still show some `tapClientLookup: Index N out of bounds (length: M)` failures escaping from `UserMessage` to `[error-boundary:root]`. Without the root recovery fallback, a transient one-frame inconsistency can strand the entire Desktop on the error screen even though the next render against the current store snapshot would succeed.

This issue tracks the **regression in the root-level mitigation**, not the underlying assistant-ui race. The broader race remains tracked by #45403.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use current `main` at `226e8de827a669e8ffa7035b27d70c19e44b1208`.
2. Render the Desktop root `ErrorBoundary` with a child that throws:

   ```text
   tapClientLookup: Index 6 out of bounds (length: 2)
   ```

3. Clear the transient condition before the next task and advance timers.
4. Observe that the boundary remains on its root fallback because no automatic recovery is scheduled.

A focused component regression test reproduces this deterministically: it fails on untouched current `main` and passes when the bounded root recovery is restored.

## Expected Behavior

For this exact transient error class, the root boundary should schedule a bounded next-tick retry so React can reconcile against the latest store snapshot. Recovery must be root-only and capped so persistent errors still expose the normal fallback.

## Actual Behavior

The current root boundary only records the error and renders its fallback. It has no automatic recovery path, so the entire Desktop remains unavailable until the user retries or reloads.

## Affected Component

Hermes Desktop (`apps/desktop`)

## Debug Report

Not published. No private runtime data is required to establish this source regression; the current file history and deterministic component test reproduce it directly.

## Operating System

CachyOS Linux

## Hermes Revision

`226e8de827a669e8ffa7035b27d70c19e44b1208`

## Root Cause Analysis

#52704 merged bounded root recovery in commit `2e3efce66ebd0a144a0733333e1c0d31d9f65c5d`. Later, #49037 (`344415892f5d1de80fe4141e4ba3dfb76d167124`) restored the earlier `error-boundary.tsx` implementation and removed its regression tests while landing unrelated shared project UI work. Current `main` therefore contains the message-local mitigation but no root-level safety net for escaping lookup races.

## Proposed Fix

Restore a narrower version of the bounded recovery:

- match only the exact `tapClientLookup: Index ... out of bounds (length: ...)` message;
- enable it only for the root boundary;
- allow at most three retries in five seconds;
- clear pending timers on unmount/reset;
- retain the existing fallback for scoped, unrelated, and persistent errors.

## Pull Request

A focused two-file fix with behavior tests is available in #64310.

items.title: [Bug]: Non-standard JSON Schema type strings (e.g. "type": "custom") in tool parameters cause HTTP 400 on Anthropic API

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

When an MCP server's tool schema contains a non-standard JSON Schema `type` value (e.g. `"type": "custom"`) in a nested `properties` field, Hermes passes it through to the LLM backend. The Anthropic API validates tool schemas against the JSON Schema metaschema and rejects any `type` value not in the primitive set (`object`, `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array`, `null`), returning HTTP 400. This blocks the entire conversation — every request fails immediately, non-retryable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with a model using `api_mode: anthropic_messages` (e.g. `claude-glm-5.2`)
2. Connect an MCP server whose tool schema includes `"type": "custom"` in a nested property
3. Send any message
4. Request fails immediately with HTTP 400

## Expected Behavior

Hermes sanitizes non-standard type strings before sending to the API, coercing them to a valid JSON Schema type.

## Actual Behavior

The invalid type string reaches the upstream API unchanged, causing HTTP 400:
```
Tool 0 function has invalid 'parameters' schema: 'custom' is not valid under any of the given schemas
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`_sanitize_node()` in `tools/schema_sanitizer.py` (line ~289) handles `key == "type"` only when the value is a **list** (type arrays, lines 289–306). When `value` is a string like `"custom"`, it falls through to the generic `else` branch (line ~335) which passes strings through unchanged: `out[key] = value`. The Anthropic adapter's `_normalize_tool_input_schema()` in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` (line ~1621) also lacks recursive type-string validation.

Reproduced with a direct curl: sending `input_schema.properties.mode.type = "custom"` to `/v1/messages` produces the exact same 400. Replacing `"custom"` with `"string"` succeeds (200 OK).

## Proposed Fix

Two layers, both in Hermes Python:
- **Layer 1** (`_sanitize_node()` in `tools/schema_sanitizer.py`): validate string `type` values against the JSON Schema primitive set; coerce unrecognized values to `"object"`. Runs for all API modes.
- **Layer 2** (`_normalize_tool_input_schema()` in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py`): add recursive `_coerce_invalid_types()` helper as defense-in-depth for the Anthropic path.

items.title: Compaction resets Hindsight turn buffer without flushing pending memories

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
## Problem

Context compression (compaction) resets the Hindsight memory provider's turn buffer without flushing pending retains first, causing conversation turns to be silently lost at the compaction boundary.

### Call chain

```
compaction fires → conversation_compression.py:906
  → on_session_switch(reason="compression")
  → Hindsight plugin clears: _session_turns=[], _turn_counter=0, _last_retained_turn_count=0
```

`MemoryManager.flush_pending()` exists (line 668) but is **never called** on the compaction path. The method is documented as being "used at real session boundaries" but compaction is not wired up to use it.

### Additional issue

`flush_min_turns` exists in `cli-config.yaml.example` (line 563) but is **never read by any Python code** — it is a no-op configuration key.

## Reproduction

1. Configure Hindsight as memory provider (`memory.provider: hindsight`)
2. Run a long session with `compression.threshold: 0.75` (default)
3. Compaction triggers (check logs for "Preflight compression")
4. After compaction, check Hindsight container logs for `batch_retain` entries
5. Observe that retain activity stops or gaps after the compaction timestamp

## Root cause

`conversation_compression.py` line ~906 calls `on_session_switch()` directly without first calling `agent._memory_manager.flush_pending(timeout=5.0)`. Any `sync_all()` dispatched after the last successful retain but before compaction fires is associated with the old session document, and when `on_session_switch` clears the buffer, those pending turns are lost.

## Proposed fix

In `conversation_compression.py`, before calling `on_session_switch` (line ~906):

```python
# Flush pending memory retains before compaction boundary
try:
    if agent._memory_manager:
        agent._memory_manager.flush_pending(timeout=5.0)
except Exception as _fp_err:
    logger.debug("memory flush before compaction: %s", _fp_err)

try:
    if _is_boundary and agent._memory_manager:
        agent._memory_manager.on_session_switch(...)
```

Also consider removing `flush_min_turns` from `cli-config.yaml.example` as it is not referenced by any Python code.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: git `local/customizations` branch
- Hindsight: local_external mode, Docker container
- Model: Qwen3.6-27B local (262K context)
- Compression: threshold 0.75, target_ratio 0.1

In `sanitize_api_messages()`, the deduplication pass that removes duplicate `tool_call_id`s (#58327) can produce an empty `tool_calls: []` array on an assistant message when ALL of its tool calls are deduped. Strict providers (DeepSeek v4, newer OpenAI) reject this with HTTP 400:

```
Invalid 'messages[N].tool_calls': empty array. Expected an array with minimum length 1, but got an empty array instead.
```

## Root cause

The existing first-pass fix for empty arrays (#58755, #5737) covers messages that already *store* `tool_calls: []` on disk, but it runs **before** the dedup pass. When the dedup pass (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` ~line 2600) removes every tool_call from a message because all IDs were already seen earlier in the same request, it writes:

```python
msg = {**msg, "tool_calls": kept_tcs}  # kept_tcs == [] → tool_calls: []
```

This newly-created `tool_calls: []` is never caught by any later sanitizer stage.

## Reproduction conditions

- Long sessions (200+ messages) where the same `tool_call_id` string appears on multiple assistant messages across different turns
- The agent sends the full history as `conversation_history` in one shot (WebUI pattern; TUI accumulates incrementally, so it is unaffected)
- Affects both direct DeepSeek and opencode-go providers

## Fix

When `kept_tcs` is empty after dedup, drop the `tool_calls` key entirely instead of writing an empty list:

```python
if kept_tcs:
    msg = {**msg, "tool_calls": kept_tcs}
else:
    msg = {k: v for k, v in msg.items() if k != "tool_calls"}
```

## Regression scope

Introduced by #58327 (tool_call_id dedup). The earlier fixes #58755 / #5737 were insufficient because they only sanitize the *input* to sanitize_api_messages, not the intermediate state produced by the dedup pass itself.

items.title: mem0 plugin: group chat memory stored under wrong user_id due to agent cache reuse

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Problem

In a Feishu (Lark) group chat, when user A sends a message to the bot and the bot calls `mem0_conclude` (or `mem0_add` in latest version), the memory is stored under user B's `user_id` instead of user A's.

## Root Cause

1. The `mem0_conclude` / `mem0_add` tool has no `user_id` parameter — it always uses `self._user_id` which is set once during `initialize()`.

2. `self._user_id` is resolved as: `kwargs.get("user_id") or self._config.get("user_id", "hermes-user")`

3. When the gateway caches an agent instance (see `gateway/run.py` cached agent logic around line 10635-10639), the cached agent retains the `user_id` from the previous session. If user A's DM session created the agent, and then a group chat message from user B reuses that cached agent, `self._user_id` is still user A's ID.

4. Even without caching, `mem0.json` has a hardcoded `user_id` (e.g., the bot admin's ID), which becomes the fallback when `source.user_id` is empty.

## Impact

- Memories from group chats are attributed to the wrong user
- When user B later queries their memories, they see user A's memories and vice versa
- Memory isolation between users in group chat scenarios is broken

## Reproduction

1. Configure `mem0.json` with a fixed `user_id` (e.g., bot admin's open_id)
2. User A sends a message in DM → bot calls `mem0_conclude` → stored under user A's ID ✓
3. User B sends a message in a group chat → bot calls `mem0_conclude` → stored under user A's ID ✗

## Suggested Fix

Option A: Add an optional `user_id` parameter to `mem0_conclude` / `mem0_add`, defaulting to `self._user_id` but allowing the agent to override it with the actual message sender's ID (available via `self._user_id` in AIAgent which comes from `source.user_id`).

Option B: Ensure the cached agent's `user_id` is updated per-turn to match the current message sender, rather than being frozen at agent creation time.

## Environment

- hermes-agent version: v2026.4.23
- Also checked latest main (v2026.7.7.2-531-g89bd0fba9) — issue still present
- Platform: Feishu (Lark) group chat
- Memory backend: self-hosted mem0 server

items.title: [Bug]: `hermes update` silently removes root-only npm deps (agent-browser) on every run

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
### Bug Description

Every `hermes update` removes the repo-root npm dependencies — including `agent-browser` — while printing `✓ repo root + ui-tui, web workspaces (desktop skipped)`. Browser tools stay broken until the user manually runs `npm install agent-browser` in the install dir. The update exits 0, so nothing signals that anything went wrong.

Reproduces on every update. Install method `git`, on `main`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install via `git` method on Linux, on `main`.
2. Run `hermes update`.
3. `ls node_modules/agent-browser` in the install dir → **gone**.
4. Browser tools fail until `npm install agent-browser` is run manually.

Minimal isolated repro (root + workspace manifests + lockfile copied out of a checkout; `--ignore-scripts` for speed), replaying exactly what the updater runs:

```console
$ npm ci --no-fund --no-audit --progress=false --ignore-scripts --workspaces=false
exit=0
agent-browser present after step 1: YES

$ npm ci --no-fund --no-audit --progress=false --ignore-scripts --workspace ui-tui --workspace web
exit=0
agent-browser present after step 2: NO      # <-- wiped, exit 0
```

Note: `npm ci --dry-run` does **not** reveal this — it reports a delta against the existing `node_modules` rather than simulating the wipe, so it misleadingly shows nothing being removed. Only a real run exposes it.

### Expected Behavior

After `hermes update`, `node_modules` contains the repo-root dependencies (`agent-browser`, `@streamdown`) plus the ui-tui and web workspaces, with `apps/desktop`/Electron still skipped. Browser tools keep working with no manual `npm install`.

If the install tree ends up incomplete, `hermes update` should say so rather than print `✓`.

### Actual Behavior

`node_modules` is left without the root-only deps. `agent-browser` is absent, so browser tools break. The update reports success:

```
→ Updating Node.js dependencies...
  ✓ repo root + ui-tui, web workspaces (desktop skipped)
...
✓ Update complete!
```

Workaround each time:

```console
$ cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent && npm install agent-browser
```

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A

### Debug Report

```shell
Omitted deliberately — on this install `hermes debug share` emits a live
credential into its output, so I'm not willing to put it on a public paste.
Filed separately: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/64351
```

Everything needed to reproduce this bug is above and doesn't depend on the bundle.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (x86_64)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

`main` @ `226e8de827a669e8ffa7035b27d70c19e44b1208` (2026-07-13) — install method: `git`; npm 10.9.8 / Node v22.22.3

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`_update_node_dependencies()` (`hermes_cli/main.py:8146-8188`) installs Node deps in two passes to avoid pulling Electron via `apps/desktop`:

1. `npm install --workspaces=false` → root deps (`agent-browser`, `@streamdown`)
2. `npm install --workspace ui-tui --workspace web` → only those workspaces

The two-pass design assumes **additive** `npm install` semantics. But both calls go through `_run_npm_install_deterministic()` (`hermes_cli/main.py:4819-4868`), which deliberately prefers **`npm ci`**:

> Prefers ``npm ci`` (strict, lockfile-preserving) when a lockfile is present

`npm ci` **deletes `node_modules` before reifying the tree it was given**. Pass 2 is scoped by `--workspace` to ui-tui/web, so root-only deps aren't in its ideal tree — pass 2 wipes what pass 1 installed and never restores it. Both passes exit 0, so the success branch at `main.py:8184` runs and the failure is silent.

Neither piece is wrong alone; the bug is in the interaction between the two-pass caller and the helper's `npm ci` preference.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Collapse the two passes into a single `npm ci` that reifies root + the selected workspaces in one tree, via `--include-workspace-root`:

```diff
-    root_args = [*extra_args, "--workspaces=false"]
-    root_result = _run_npm_install_deterministic(
-        npm, PROJECT_ROOT, extra_args=tuple(root_args),
-        capture_output=False, env=nixos_env,
-    )
-    if root_result.returncode != 0:
-        print("  ⚠ npm install failed in repo root")
-        ...
-        return
-
-    ws_args = [*extra_args, "--workspace", "ui-tui", "--workspace", "web"]
+    ws_args = [
+        *extra_args,
+        "--workspace", "ui-tui",
+        "--workspace", "web",
+        "--include-workspace-root",
+    ]
     ws_result = _run_npm_install_deterministic(
         npm, PROJECT_ROOT, extra_args=tuple(ws_args),
         capture_output=False, env=nixos_env,
     )
```

Verified on the isolated repro — one pass, and the Electron-avoidance the two-pass design existed for is preserved:

```console
$ npm ci ... --workspace ui-tui --workspace web --include-workspace-root
exit=0
agent-browser : YES
@streamdown   : YES   (other root dep)
ui-tui deps   : YES
web deps      : YES
electron      : NO    (desktop still skipped)
```

Running this patch locally now; happy to open a PR if useful.

**Hardening suggestion:** even with the fix, a scoped `npm ci` silently pruning root deps is easy to reintroduce. Consider asserting the tree is complete after install (e.g. each root `dependencies` entry resolves) and failing loudly instead of printing `✓`.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop MoA incomplete-slot autosave corrupts settings; hermes update on Windows wipes local fix and reintroduces bug

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

Hermes Desktop Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) settings editor corrupts user edits when a reference/aggregator **provider is changed before a model is selected**.

### What happens
1. User adds a MoA reference model, or changes an existing reference/aggregator provider.
2. The UI clears `model` to empty while waiting for the user to pick a model.
3. Debounced autosave (~600ms) persists the incomplete slot.
4. Backend normalization drops empty-model slots and falls back to hardcoded defaults (commonly OpenRouter).
5. The server response overwrites the editor state, so:
   - the newly added reference **disappears**, and/or
   - aggregator provider **jumps to OpenRouter**.

### Critical regression: official update wipes local fix
We applied a verified local Plan B fix that solved the bug. After running `hermes update` / Desktop updater against `main`, the fix was **stashed, conflicted, and discarded** by the updater’s “reset to remote main / clean working tree” path. The bug immediately returned until the local fix was re-applied.

This means Windows users cannot rely on local hotfixes across updates. Upstream needs an official fix merged to `main`.

Related existing issues/PRs (not yet merged as of this report):
- #63658
- #64156
- PR #63867
- PR #64158

## Steps to Reproduce

### A. Original UI bug (Desktop MoA editor)
1. Open Hermes Desktop.
2. Go to **Settings → Model → Mixture of Agents**.
3. Click **Add reference model**.
4. On the new row, open the **provider** selector and choose a non-OpenRouter provider (e.g. DeepSeek / custom provider).
5. Do **not** immediately select a model; wait >600ms.
6. Observe: the new reference row disappears and/or provider reverts to OpenRouter defaults.

Repeat for aggregator:
1. Change Aggregator provider to DeepSeek (or other non-default provider).
2. Wait >600ms without selecting model.
3. Observe: aggregator jumps back to OpenRouter default.

### B. Update overwrite / fix regression (Windows, source install)
1. Apply a local fix for the above bug to:
   - `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/model-settings.tsx`
   - `hermes_cli/web_server.py`
   - rebuild Desktop pack (`win-unpacked`)
2. Confirm MoA editor works (incomplete provider/model drafts stay local).
3. Run official update:
   - Desktop: **Update Hermes** / `hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main`
   - or CLI: `hermes update`
4. Observe updater log pattern:
   - local changes stashed
   - history diverged → reset to remote main
   - restore stash conflicts (e.g. on `model-settings.test.tsx`)
   - working tree reset to clean state
5. After update + restart, re-open MoA settings.
6. Observe: original bug returns because local Plan B patch is gone.

## Expected Behavior
- Changing provider before model selection should keep a **local draft**.
- Incomplete slots (`provider` set, `model` empty) must **not** autosave.
- Incomplete slots must **not** be normalized into hardcoded OpenRouter defaults.
- Selecting model after provider should then save complete payload.
- Official updates should not silently destroy local verified fixes without a clear recovery path; ideally the bug is fixed on `main` so local patching is unnecessary.

## Actual Behavior
- Incomplete MoA slots are autosaved after ~600ms.
- Backend drops empty-model slots and substitutes defaults.
- UI overwrites local draft from server response → rows disappear / provider jumps to OpenRouter.
- After official update, local Plan B fix is removed and the bug returns.

## Root Cause (source-level)

### Desktop UI
`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/model-settings.tsx`:
- provider change forces `model = ''`
- `scheduleMoaSave` debounces 600ms and calls `saveMoaModels(next)` even when incomplete
- response replaces local state

### Backend
`hermes_cli/moa_config.py` / `web_server.py` PUT `/api/model/moa`:
- incomplete slots cleaned out (`_clean_slot`)
- empty preset falls back to default OpenRouter aggregator/reference models

### Update path (why recurrence happens)
Windows updater (`hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main`) when local changes diverge:
1. stash local changes
2. reset to remote main
3. restore stash → conflict
4. reset working tree to clean remote state
5. rebuild/activate Desktop from clean main content stamp

Result: any unmerged local MoA fix is wiped.

## Timeline / Evidence (this machine)

### 2026-07-13 — bug found, Plan B fixed it
- Bug reproduced on Desktop MoA settings.
- Local Plan B implemented and verified:
  - incomplete drafts stay local
  - complete slots save
  - concurrent saves serialized
  - incomplete PUT rejected with 422
- Deployed successfully:
  - install stamp commit `12922087eae7ea6eac41672bd3fd3148ff4acf6d`
  - branch `fix/moa-desktop-draft-safety`
- User confirmed MoA settings worked after deploy/restart.

### 2026-07-14 morning — official update reintroduced bug
`bootstrap-installer.log` (excerpt):
```text
2026-07-14T09:21:00 [update] updating against branch main
→ Local changes detected — stashing before update...
→ Found 1 new commit(s)
  ⚠ Fast-forward not possible (history diverged), resetting to match remote...
→ Restoring local changes...
✗ Update pulled new code, but restoring local changes hit conflicts.
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in apps/desktop/src/app/settings/model-settings.test.tsx
Working tree reset to clean state.
Restore your changes later with: git stash apply db5cd228efaa...
✓ Code updated!
builtAt / install stamp moved back to main
```

After update:
- formal `model-settings.tsx` no longer contained Plan B gates
- formal `web_server.py` no longer contained incomplete-slot 422 validator
- install stamp returned to main (`226e8de...` at that time)
- MoA settings bug returned immediately

### 2026-07-14 evening — re-applied Plan B, fixed again
- Created pre-reapply snapshot first.
- Re-deployed Plan B from verified candidate package.
- Deploy log:
```text
[2026-07-14 18:38:46] Plan B deploy completed successfully
```
- Current formal install stamp again:
```json
{
  "commit": "12922087eae7ea6eac41672bd3fd3148ff4acf6d",
  "branch": "fix/moa-desktop-draft-safety",
  "builtAt": "2026-07-13T12:24:41.333Z"
}
```
- Fix markers present again in formal source/package.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19045.6093)
- Python: 3.11.15
- Hermes: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), git install
- Install dir: `C:\Users\ASUS\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent`
- Desktop: packaged `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked`
- Platform: Desktop settings (not gateway-only)

## Affected Component
- Desktop MoA settings editor
- Desktop update/rebuild pipeline (Windows source install)
- `/api/model/moa` save normalization path

## What official fix should do
1. **Do not autosave incomplete MoA slots** (provider without model).
2. Keep incomplete rows as local drafts until complete.
3. Reject incomplete writes with 422 (or ignore incomplete slots without replacing entire preset with defaults).
4. Serialize concurrent MoA saves; ignore stale responses.
5. Clear pending autosaves on profile switch.
6. Merge the fix to `main` so `hermes update` does not reintroduce the bug.
7. Optional: when update stash restore conflicts, preserve a recoverable backup path that does not silently drop user-validated local patches without warning.

## Debug Report
`hermes debug share` was not uploaded from this session (automated agent environment). Key local evidence available:
- deploy log: Plan B completed successfully on 2026-07-14 18:38:46
- bootstrap installer log: 2026-07-14 09:21 update stash/reset/conflict sequence
- source markers before/after update and re-apply
- formal vs candidate SHA comparison

If needed I can provide redacted log excerpts or a local `hermes debug share --local` dump.

## Additional Notes
- This is **not** caused by adding custom providers (e.g. via CC Switch). Custom providers only expose more provider options; the disappearance/jump is caused by incomplete-slot autosave + normalization + update overwrite of the local fix.
- Existing PRs (#63867, #64158) appear to target the same class of bug but were **not merged** at the time this recurrence happened; please prioritize merging an official fix so Windows users do not need repeated local Plan B redeploys after every update.

items.title: [Bug] Web provider plugins fail to load — plugins/web added to sys.path shadows PyPI packages firecrawl/ddgs; all 7 web backends fail to register

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary
After the 2026-07-09 update that restructured web backends into \`plugins/web/<name>/\` plugin packages, **all web search/extract backends fail to load**. The plugin loader adds \`plugins/web\` to \`sys.path\` as a top-level entry, which (a) shadows PyPI packages whose name equals the plugin directory (\`firecrawl\`, \`ddgs\`), and (b) breaks the \`plugins.web.<name>\` import path the loader itself uses — so every web plugin reports \`No module named 'plugins.web.<name>'\` and never registers.

Net effect: \`web_search\` / \`web_extract\` are broken for **every** backend except those that happen to import a differently-named dependency (\`tavily\` → \`httpx\`, \`exa\` → \`exa_py\`).

## Environment
- Hermes Agent (fork \`luxles/hermes-agent\`), updated 2026-07-09
- Python 3.12.3 (WSL)
- venv: \`/home/luxles/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv\`
- \`firecrawl\` SDK **4.17.0** is correctly installed in the venv: \`venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/firecrawl/\`
- \`web.backend\` / \`search_backend\` / \`extract_backend\` = \`firecrawl\` (or \`ddgs\`, etc.)

## Reproduction (runtime, not simulated)
Run the loader exactly as Hermes does, then inspect import resolution:

\`\`\`python
# venv/bin/python
from hermes_cli.plugins import _ensure_plugins_discovered
_ensure_plugins_discovered(force=True)

import sys, importlib.util
print([p for p in sys.path if "plugins" in p])
# -> ['/home/luxles/.hermes/hermes-agent/plugins/web',
#     '/home/luxles/.hermes/plugins/web']

print(importlib.util.find_spec("firecrawl").origin)
# -> /home/luxles/.hermes/hermes-agent/plugins/web/firecrawl/__init__.py   (shadowed)
\`\`\`

The same \`force=True\` call also prints, for **all 7** web providers:

\`\`\`
Failed to load plugin 'web-firecrawl': No module named 'plugins.web.firecrawl'
Failed to load plugin 'web-ddgs':      No module named 'plugins.web.ddgs'
Failed to load plugin 'web-exa':       No module named 'plugins.web.exa'
Failed to load plugin 'web-tavily':    No module named 'plugins.web.tavily'
Failed to load plugin 'web-parallel':  No module named 'plugins.web.parallel'
Failed to load plugin 'web-searxng':   No module named 'plugins.web.searxng'
Failed to load plugin 'web-brave-free':No module named 'plugins.web.brave_free'
Failed to load plugin 'web-xai':       No module named 'plugins.web.xai'
\`\`\`

After this, any \`web_search\` / \`web_extract\` call fails:
- backend \`firecrawl\` → \`cannot import name 'Firecrawl' from 'firecrawl' (.../plugins/web/firecrawl/__init__.py)\`
- backend \`ddgs\` → \`cannot import name 'DDGS' from 'ddgs' (.../plugins/web/ddgs/__init__.py)\`

## Root cause
The plugin discovery path (\`hermes_cli/plugins.py\` → \`PluginManager.discover_and_load\` → \`_discover_and_load_inner\`) adds \`plugins/web\` (both the repo copy and the user copy \`~/.hermes/plugins/web\`) to \`sys.path\` as a **top-level** entry during loading.

Two consequences, both fatal:

1. **Name shadowing (firecrawl / ddgs).** With \`plugins/web\` on \`sys.path\`, the subdirectory \`firecrawl/\` becomes the top-level importable name \`firecrawl\`, shadowing \`site-packages/firecrawl\`. \`from firecrawl import Firecrawl\` resolves to \`plugins/web/firecrawl/__init__.py\` (which only defines \`register()\`), not the real SDK → \`ImportError\`. Same for \`ddgs\` (\`from ddgs import DDGS\`).

2. **Self-breaking import path (all 7).** The loader imports each provider via \`plugins.web.<name>\` (e.g. \`web_tools.py:53\` does \`from plugins.web.firecrawl.provider import ...\`). But once \`plugins/web\` is a top-level path, \`plugins\` is no longer the parent package of \`plugins.web.<name>\` — so \`import plugins.web.firecrawl\` fails with \`No module named 'plugins.web.firecrawl'\`, and the plugin never registers. This is why **all 7** web backends fail to load, not just the name-colliding ones.

**Positive control — proves it is the \`sys.path\` insertion, not the SDK:** with \`plugins/web\` *not* on \`sys.path\`, the real package resolves correctly:
\`\`\`python
# fresh interpreter, no discovery run
import importlib.util
importlib.util.find_spec("firecrawl").origin
# -> .../venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/firecrawl/__init__.py   (OK)
\`\`\`

**Positive control — proves it is name collision, not a general break:** providers that import a *differently-named* dependency work fine end-to-end:
- \`tavily\` imports \`httpx\` directly (no \`tavily\` package) → search + extract OK
- \`exa\` imports \`exa_py\` (not \`exa\`) → search + extract OK

Only \`firecrawl\` and \`ddgs\` (directory name == imported PyPI package name) hit the shadowing path.

## Regression evidence
The pre-update snapshot \`state-snapshots/20260709-002046-pre-update/\` contains **no \`plugins/web/\` directory**; the prior config used \`web-search-router\` and the old inline implementation in \`tools/web_tools.py\`. The 2026-07-09 update restructured web backends into \`plugins/web/<name>/\` plugin packages (confirmed by \`tools/web_tools.py\` comments referencing \`plugins/web/firecrawl/provider.py\`, etc.). The new layout is what introduces both failure modes above.

## Impact
- \`firecrawl\` and \`ddgs\` backends: completely broken (shadowing ImportError).
- All 7 bundled web plugins: fail to even register during discovery (\`No module named 'plugins.web.<name>'\`), so they are unavailable regardless of config. The only backends that function are those whose providers import a non-colliding dependency (\`tavily\`, \`exa\`).
- Distinct from the "silent failure / no actionable error" reports (#58320, #60425): the error here is explicit, but the backend is still non-functional. It is also a deeper instance of the plugin-loading breakage described in #27683 (missing \`_ensure_plugins_discovered()\` at dispatch sites) — here discovery runs but self-sabotages via \`sys.path\`.

## Workaround
Use a backend whose provider does not collide with a top-level package name: \`tavily\` (httpx) or \`exa\` (\`exa_py\`). Both search and extract work through these.

## Suggested fix (non-exhaustive)
The loader must not put \`plugins/web\` (or any per-category subdir) on \`sys.path\` as a top-level entry. Options:
- Load provider modules via \`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location\` against the absolute \`provider.py\` path (no \`sys.path\` mutation), keeping \`plugins.web.<name>\` resolvable through the repo package; **or**
- Rename the plugin directories so they never collide with an installed package (e.g. \`plugins/web/firecrawl_provider/\`, \`plugins/web/ddgs_provider/\`) and update \`plugin.yaml\` \`provides_web_providers\` + loader references; **or**
- Insert \`site-packages\` ahead of \`plugins/web\` on \`sys.path\` so the real PyPI package wins name collisions.

(See also cross-reference comment on #58320 — different root cause, tracked here separately.)

## Bug description

`hermes curator status` labels its table as “agent-created skills,” but with the default `curator.prune_builtins: true`, the table also contains bundled built-in skills.

On a profile with zero usage records marked `created_by: agent` or `agent_created: true`, the command reported 71 “agent-created” skills. Those 71 were the 72 bundled names minus the protected `plan` skill.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a profile with bundled skills seeded and no agent-created skill records.
2. Leave `curator.prune_builtins` at its default `true`.
3. Run `hermes -p <profile> curator status`.
4. Compare the reported “agent-created skills” count with `hermes -p <profile> curator usage` and the bundled manifest.

## Expected behavior

The status output should say “curator-managed skills” and distinguish agent-created from bundled-pruning candidates, or otherwise label each provenance accurately.

## Actual behavior

The CLI calls `agent_created_report()` and prints “agent-created skills,” even though that report intentionally includes bundled built-ins whenever `prune_builtins` is enabled.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: `v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)`
- Verified unchanged on current repository `main`: `adf62065a73fa9682917053dd55197f63c4a43e4`
- OS: macOS 26.4
- Hermes runtime Python: 3.11.14

## Root cause

- `tools/skill_usage.py::list_agent_created_skill_names()` explicitly includes bundled skills when `prune_builtins` is true.
- `tools/skill_usage.py::agent_created_report()` therefore returns all curator-managed candidates, not only agent-created skills.
- `hermes_cli/curator.py` prints “no agent-created skills” / the agent-created heading for that mixed-provenance result.

## Proposed fix

Rename the CLI section and internal report to “curator-managed skills,” include a provenance column/count, and retain a separate agent-created-only count if useful. Add a regression test for a fresh profile with `prune_builtins` both on and off.

items.title: Factory orchestration: stay on delegate_task until we need multiple worker profiles
items.body:
## Context

We're running a multi-repo software factory (19 private repos, 239 open issues) on a single `default` Hermes profile. Today the orchestration stack is:

- **GitHub issues + labels** (`0-to-plan`, `1-agent-ready`, `2-in-progress`, `pr:pending-mcu`) = our board
- **`delegate_task`** = ephemeral parallel work
- **Cron + `factory-status.sh`** = scheduled sweeps and on-demand status DMs
- **Factory protocol**: Hermes never merges PRs itself; merges dispatch to vendor agents (Cursor, Claude Code) or the human via `/mcu`

We've been contemplating whether to adopt Hermes Kanban as the orchestration layer. This issue captures the analysis for future reference.

## Pros: Kanban Fits Because...

- **True process isolation** — workers are independent Hermes profile processes, not child coroutines. If the gateway crashes, the SQLite board survives and workers resume.
- **Git worktree concurrency** — with 19 repos, parallel agents editing the same repo via `delegate_task` causes git lock errors. Kanban workers use worktrees (`-w`) automatically.
- **Structured dispatch + auto-retry** — dispatcher routes tasks by worker `--description`, auto-blocks after N failures, reclaims stale claims.
- **Durable work queue as source of truth** — `ready → claimed → blocked → completed` is persisted in SQLite, separate from session history.

## Cons: Friction Points

- **Split-brain state (biggest risk)** — GitHub labels already function as our board. Adding Hermes Kanban creates **two** boards that must be kept in sync (e.g., "kanban claim = add `2-in-progress` label"). Without sync automation, they drift.
- **Memory & protocol silos** — A freshly created `coder` worker profile doesn't inherit the `default` profile's memory. Worker-specific strict protocols (never-merge rule, verbatim relay for `dm_text`, `awaiting_human_merge` attestation) must be manually seeded via SOUL.md + memory per profile.
- **Merge protocol collision** — Kanban's default model is `claim → work → complete (PR merged)`. Our factory forbids host-side merging; workers must stop at `PR opened, awaiting MCU` and block. We'd need to redefine "completion" semantics.
- **Operational overhead** — multiple `.env` files, multiple gateway services (if separate Slack identities), multiple skill trees to keep synced via curator.

## Decision (2026-07-14)

**Stay on the current stack.** `delegate_task` + GitHub labels + cron is sufficient until we actually need multiple *persistent* worker agent roles (beyond the single orchestrator).

## Graduation Triggers (when to revisit Kanban)

We should adopt Kanban when **any** of these become true:

1. We need persistent, long-lived worker agents doing autonomous multi-hour work that must outlive the parent session
2. We have 3+ distinct worker roles (`coder`, `reviewer`, `researcher`, etc.) that need independent SOULs and memory contexts
3. We need multiple workers hammering the same repo simultaneously and worktrees-via-delegate aren't enough
4. We want to decouple the orchestrator from worker execution so this DM stays responsive while heavy codegen runs in the background

## Related

- Hermes profiles docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/profiles
- Kanban docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/kanban
- Origin Slack thread: Profile capabilities discussion (2026-07-14)

Tracking this so we have a future reference point when we *do* hit the graduation triggers.

items.title: [Bug]: MoA reference models receive empty content when aggregator uses prompt caching (cache_control converts string to list)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a MoA preset's aggregator is a **Claude model** (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` via `nous`), `apply_anthropic_cache_control()` converts each message's `content` from a plain string to a list format (`[{"type": "text", "text": "...", "cache_control": {...}}]`). The `_reference_messages()` function in `agent/moa_loop.py` only handles string content — for list content it falls through to an empty string, causing **all reference models to receive empty user messages**.

The aggregator still works (it receives the full untrimmed messages), so the MoA output looks normal — but the multi-model cross-validation value is silently destroyed. Every reference returns variations of "no conversation state was provided" or "no task context provided".

## Root Cause

**Bug chain:**

1. `agent_init.py` L606: `provider=moa` → `_anthropic_prompt_cache_policy()` resolves the aggregator slot → finds a Claude model → returns `(True, False)` → `_use_prompt_caching = True`
2. `conversation_loop.py` L889-894: `apply_anthropic_cache_control()` executes → `_apply_cache_marker()` (prompt_caching.py L40-44) converts `content` from `string` to `list` format
3. `moa_loop.py` L845: `MoAClient.create()` receives messages where `content` is now a list
4. `moa_loop.py` L473: `_reference_messages()` does `text = content if isinstance(content, str) else ""` → `text = ""` (empty)
5. Reference model receives empty user message → returns "no conversation state"

## Reproduction

```bash
# Triggers the bug (aggregator = nous/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, prompt caching enabled)
hermes chat -q "What is 1+1?" -m tech-council --provider moa -Q --max-turns 1

# Does NOT trigger (aggregator = zai/glm-5.2, prompt caching disabled)
hermes chat -q "What is 1+1?" -m quick-council --provider moa -Q --max-turns 1
```

### Reference output before fix (tech-council):
```
Reference 1/3 — aicodewith/glm-5.2: "no conversation state or task context was provided"
Reference 2/3 — deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro: [answers an unrelated question]
Reference 3/3 — minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3: "no actual task or context provided"
```

### Reference output after fix (tech-council):
```
Reference 1/3 — aicodewith/glm-5.2: "1+1等于2" ✅
Reference 2/3 — deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro: "1+1等于2" ✅
Reference 3/3 — minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3: [correct reasoning] ✅
```

## Impact

- **Severity**: High — silently destroys MoA's core value proposition (multi-model reference cross-validation)
- **Affected presets**: Any MoA preset whose aggregator triggers prompt caching (Claude models on native Anthropic, OpenRouter, or third-party Anthropic-compatible gateways)
- **Non-affected**: Presets with non-Claude aggregators (e.g. zai/glm-5.2) where `_use_prompt_caching = False`
- **Duration**: Since prompt caching was added for MoA aggregators (the `_anthropic_prompt_cache_policy` MoA-aware resolver at `agent_runtime_helpers.py` L1530-1562)

## Fix

`agent/moa_loop.py`, function `_reference_messages()`, line 473:

```python
# Before (buggy):
text = content if isinstance(content, str) else ""

# After (fixed):
if isinstance(content, str):
    text = content
elif isinstance(content, list):
    text = " ".join(
        part.get("text", "") if isinstance(part, dict) else str(part)
        for part in content
    ).strip()
else:
    text = ""
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Upstream commit: 2d0f2185
- Install method: git
- OS: Windows 10
- MoA preset: tech-council (3 refs: glm-5.2 + deepseek-v4-pro + MiniMax-M3, aggregator: nous/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5)

items.title: Dashboard auto-SSO redirect breaks for basic_auth (password-only) providers

labels.name: duplicate

labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
### Describe the bug

When `dashboard.basic_auth` (the username/password auth provider) is configured as the **only** auth provider, accessing any protected page on the Dashboard (port 9119) triggers an HTTP 500 error.

The auto-SSO redirect sends the browser to `/auth/login?provider=basic&next=...` instead of `/login` (the password login form), and `BasicAuthProvider.start_login()` raises `NotImplementedError` because it is password-only — it has no OAuth redirect flow.

### To Reproduce

1. Configure basic auth in `config.yaml`:
```yaml
dashboard:
  basic_auth:
    username: admin
    password_hash: ...
```
2. Restart the dashboard
3. Open `http://localhost:9119` in a browser
4. **Expected**: See the password login form at `/login`
5. **Actual**: Redirected to `/auth/login?provider=basic&next=...` → 500 error page

### Root Cause

`_auto_sso_response()` in `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py` is designed for OAuth providers (silent redirect to the IdP). When exactly one provider is registered, it assumes it's an OAuth provider and redirects to `/auth/login?provider=...`. `BasicAuthProvider` has `supports_password = True` and `start_login()` raises `NotImplementedError`, producing a 500.

```python
# Line ~180 in middleware.py
providers = list_session_providers()
if len(providers) != 1:
    return None
# ↓ reaches here for password-only providers
provider = providers[0]
# ... builds /auth/login?provider=... URL
```

### Fix

Skip auto-SSO when the single provider is password-only:

```python
provider = providers[0]
if getattr(provider, 'supports_password', False):
    return None  # password-only provider, show /login form instead
```

### Environment

- Hermes Agent version: 0.18.2
- Dashboard with basic_auth (password-only, no OAuth)
- OS: Linux

### Additional context

Introduced when `_auto_sso_response` was added for OAuth SSO convenience. It never considered password-only providers. v0.17.x did not have this issue.

items.body:
### Describe the bug

On the Web Dashboard (port 9119), clicking a past session in the sidebar (right-side session list on the Chat page) changes the heading to the session title but **does not display the previous conversation messages** in the terminal. The terminal appears empty or shows the current session's content instead of the clicked session's history.

This is a regression from v0.17.x — the sidebar session switch used to work correctly via full page navigation, but the v0.18.x React SPA refactor broke it.

### To Reproduce

1. Open the Hermes Dashboard at `http://localhost:9119/chat`
2. Click a session in the right sidebar (e.g. an older conversation)
3. **Expected**: Terminal loads and displays the session's message history
4. **Actual**: Heading changes to the session title, but the terminal shows no history

### Root Cause (Backend)

When the frontend reconnects to `/api/pty` with the same `?attach=` token, `PtySessionRegistry.attach_or_spawn()` returns the **existing** PTY session, which is still running the OLD session's TUI. The new `resume=` query parameter is ignored because the existing PTY's environment (`HERMES_TUI_RESUME`) was frozen at spawn time.

A fix adds resume-change detection: when `resume` differs from the stored value, the old PTY is closed and a new one spawned with the correct `HERMES_TUI_RESUME`.

### Root Cause (Frontend)

The sidebar session click handler uses `useSearchParams().set('resume', sessionId)` with `{ replace: false }`, which only updates the URL in-place. It does NOT trigger a full React component re-mount. The WebSocket `useEffect` depends on the channel key which uses `crypto.randomUUID()` via `useMemo` — when the resume param changes, the effect re-runs and creates a new WebSocket, but there may be timing issues with the cleanup/re-creation cycle.

In contrast, the Sessions page "Resume in Chat" button uses `useNavigate('/chat?resume=SESSION_ID')` which causes a full page navigation and works correctly.

### Workaround

Use the **Sessions page** (navigate to `/sessions`, find the session, click "Resume in Chat") instead of the sidebar to switch sessions. This triggers a full navigation and works correctly.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent version: 0.18.x (regression from 0.17.x)
- Dashboard React SPA frontend
- OS: Linux

### Additional context

The backend fix alone is insufficient. The frontend sidebar click also needs to be fixed to properly trigger WebSocket reconnection with the new resume parameter.

items.title: finish_reason misclassified as "incomplete" for reasoning-only completed turns on api_mode=codex_responses (causes multi-minute stalls / iteration budget exhaustion)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
# finish_reason misclassified as "incomplete" when a completed Responses API turn's only output item is `reasoning` — causes multi-minute stalls / iteration-budget exhaustion on `api_mode: codex_responses`

## Summary

`agent/codex_responses_adapter.py::_normalize_codex_response` forces
`finish_reason = "incomplete"` whenever a turn's *only* output item is a
`reasoning` item, **even when the provider's top-level `response.status` is
`"completed"`** and there is no other signal (no `in_progress`/`queued` item
status, no error) indicating the turn is actually unfinished.

```python
elif (reasoning_items_raw or reasoning_parts or saw_reasoning_item) and not final_text:
    # Response contains only reasoning (encrypted thinking state and/or
    # human-readable summary) with no visible content or tool calls. The
    # model is still thinking and needs another turn to produce the actual
    # answer. Marking this as "stop" would send it into the empty-content
    # retry loop which burns retries then fails — treat it as incomplete so
    # the Codex continuation path handles it correctly.
    finish_reason = "incomplete"
```

This assumption ("reasoning-only output always means the model is still
thinking and will produce more") does not hold for every Responses-compatible
backend. When it's wrong, `finish_reason="incomplete"` drives
`agent/conversation_loop.py`'s continuation path
(`agent._codex_incomplete_retries < 3`), which re-issues the API call up to
3 times before giving up. Each retry re-pays the non-stream "stale call"
detector timeout, which scales up to **240s** for large-context requests
(`run_agent.py::_resolved_api_call_stale_timeout_base`,
`_compute_non_stream_stale_timeout`). Three retries at the upper bound is
**~12 minutes of wall-clock time with no visible error**, and if this
misfire repeats across multiple turns of a longer agent session, it can
burn the entire iteration budget (default 150 for interactive sessions)
while presenting only vague progress lines like:

```
Working — 6 min — iteration 93/150, waiting for non-streaming API response
Working — 9 min — iteration 136/150, receiving stream response
⚠️ Iteration budget exhausted (150/150) — asking model to summarise
```

## Where I hit this

Config: `api_mode: codex_responses` against a non-`chatgpt.com`,
non-`xai`, non-GitHub Responses-compatible relay (classified internally
as `other:<base_url>` by `_classify_responses_issuer`). Model: a
reasoning-capable GPT-5.x-class model. The relay is a legitimate
Responses API implementation, but is not one of the three backends this
file has special-cased handling for (`is_xai_responses`,
`is_github_responses`, `is_codex_backend`).

Switching the same session to `api_mode: anthropic_messages` /
`chat_completions` with a different model eliminated the symptom
immediately and repeatably — same network path, same host, same
iteration budget — which pointed at this code path rather than
network/infra.

## Minimal repro (no credentials, no network — pure unit-level repro against `_normalize_codex_response`)

```python
import sys
from types import SimpleNamespace

sys.path.insert(0, "/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent")  # adjust to your install
from agent.codex_responses_adapter import _normalize_codex_response

def make_reasoning_only_response(status="completed"):
    """A Responses API object whose ONLY output item is a completed
    'reasoning' item — no 'message', no 'function_call'. This is not a
    contrived shape: some Responses-compatible relays deliver the
    reasoning item and the final message item as separate chunks, and
    if only the reasoning chunk survives normalization for a given call
    (buffering/reordering on the relay side), this is exactly the object
    that reaches this function.
    """
    reasoning_item = SimpleNamespace(
        type="reasoning",
        status="completed",
        id="rs_repro_0001",
        encrypted_content="opaque-blob",
        summary=[SimpleNamespace(text="Thinking about the task...")],
    )
    return SimpleNamespace(
        status=status,
        output=[reasoning_item],
        output_text="",
        error=None,
    )

resp = make_reasoning_only_response(status="completed")
assistant_message, finish_reason = _normalize_codex_response(
    resp, issuer_kind="other:example-relay"
)

print("response.status (provider) :", resp.status)          # completed
print("finish_reason (Hermes)     :", finish_reason)          # incomplete  <-- BUG
assert resp.status == "completed"
assert finish_reason == "incomplete", "mismatch — see below if this ever flips"
```

Output on the version installed here:

```
response.status (provider) : completed
finish_reason (Hermes)      : incomplete
```

`response.status == "completed"` (the provider says the turn is done) but
Hermes downgrades `finish_reason` to `"incomplete"` purely because the only
output item type present is `reasoning`. There is no `in_progress`/`queued`
item, no error — nothing else in the object suggests the turn isn't
finished.

## Why this produces the exact "stuck for minutes, no error" symptom

1. `finish_reason="incomplete"` → `conversation_loop.py` hits the Codex
   continuation branch and calls `continue`, re-issuing the API request.
2. Each re-issued non-streaming call is subject to the stale-timeout
   detector, which for larger contexts is `max(stale_base, 240.0)` seconds
   (`run_agent.py::_resolved_api_call_stale_timeout_base` /
   `_compute_non_stream_stale_timeout`).
3. The continuation path retries up to 3 times
   (`agent._codex_incomplete_retries < 3`) before giving up with
   `"Codex response remained incomplete after 3 continuation attempts"`.
4. 3 × up to 240s ≈ up to 12 minutes for a *single* misfire, with only a
   generic "Working — N min — iteration X/150" status line visible to the
   user — no error, because from Hermes's perspective this is a legitimate,
   intentional retry path, not a failure.
5. If the same relay/model combination triggers this at more than one
   turn in a session, the iteration cost compounds across the whole
   session budget (default 150), producing exactly
   `⚠️ Iteration budget exhausted (150/150)`.

## Suggested fix

Don't infer "unfinished" purely from *item type composition* — trust the
provider's own `response.status` when it is unambiguous, the same way the
adjacent server-side-tool-call guard already does (comment at
`codex_responses_adapter.py` ~line 1124: server-side `*_call` items left
at `in_progress` must not flip `has_incomplete_items` when
`response.status == "completed"`). Concretely:

- When `response.status == "completed"` and there is no item at
  `queued`/`in_progress`/`incomplete` status, do not force
  `finish_reason = "incomplete"` solely because the only item type seen
  was `reasoning`. At minimum, gate the current heuristic behind
  `response_status not in {"completed"}`, mirroring the guard already used
  for `_SERVER_SIDE_TOOL_CALL_TYPES`.
- If the "reasoning-only, no visible text" case must still be retried for
  known Codex/xAI backends (where it's a documented degeneration mode),
  scope the heuristic to `is_codex_backend` / `is_xai_responses` rather
  than applying it to every `other:<base_url>` Responses-compatible
  backend, since the assumption clearly does not generalize.
- Regardless of the above, consider surfacing a distinct, more specific
  log/status line for this particular retry path (e.g. "provider returned
  reasoning with no final answer, retrying (n/3)") instead of the generic
  "Working — iteration N/150" — that alone would have cut diagnosis time
  from an hour of adapter-reading down to seconds.

## Environment

- Hermes install path: `/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent`
- `model.api_mode: codex_responses`
- Backend: third-party Responses-API-compatible relay, not one of the
  three specifically handled kinds (`is_codex_backend` /
  `is_xai_responses` / `is_github_responses`)
- Symptom reproduced consistently across multiple real chat sessions;
  switching `model.api_mode` to `anthropic_messages` with a different
  model on the same host/network eliminated it immediately.

items.title: [Bug]: Unbounded foreground terminal output can OOM and freeze the gateway before truncation

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

Foreground `terminal` output is accumulated without any runtime byte cap, then copied/scanned by post-processing before the configured output limit is applied. A verbose subprocess can therefore exhaust the gateway cgroup, drive the host into swap, and freeze Telegram/Discord/cron even though `tool_output.max_bytes` is configured.

This caused a production gateway liveness incident. The gateway process survived, but messaging stopped until Python raised `MemoryError` while processing the terminal result.

I searched existing issues/PRs and did not find one covering unbounded foreground terminal output capture.

## Steps to Reproduce

A bounded demonstration should be sufficient; do not reproduce an OOM:

1. Run Hermes gateway with the local terminal backend and the default `tool_output.max_bytes` (50,000).
2. Invoke a foreground terminal command that writes substantially more than the cap, for example a controlled 100 MiB stream:

   `python3 -c "import sys; sys.stdout.write('x' * (100 * 1024 * 1024))"`

3. Observe gateway RSS while the command runs and while its result is processed.
4. Observe that the tool response is eventually truncated to approximately 50 KB, but the complete 100 MiB string was first retained and processed in memory.

The production trigger was a `llama-cli` loading spinner piped through `tee`. Its output file reached 528,687,404 bytes (504.2 MiB).

## Expected Behavior

- Enforce the terminal output cap while draining the subprocess, not after collecting the complete stream.
- Preserve a bounded head and tail, or spool excess output to a file without retaining it in the gateway heap.
- Sudo detection, redaction, ANSI stripping, and plugin hooks should receive bounded data or a safe streamed/spooled representation.
- Excessive terminal output must not starve messaging-platform heartbeats or the gateway event loop.
- Foreground timeout enforcement should remain reliable under continuous output.

## Actual Behavior

During the production incident:

- The foreground call specified `timeout=180` but returned after 3,205.45 seconds. A separate low-volume test confirms ordinary foreground timeout handling works, so this is reported as a related continuous-output/pipeline symptom rather than a universal timeout failure.
- The gateway cgroup peaked at 3,005,456,384 bytes memory and 1,562,484,736 bytes swap.
- The kernel rejected several approximately 5.9 GiB virtual-memory allocation attempts.
- Python failed before output truncation:

```text
File "tools/terminal_tool.py", line 2672, in terminal_tool
    sudo_auth_failed = _sudo_wrong_password_failure(output)
File "tools/terminal_tool.py", line 357, in _sudo_wrong_password_failure
    lowered = output.lower()
MemoryError
```

- Discord declared its shard unresponsive and invalidated the session.
- Telegram processed queued updates only after the terminal call failed.
- Delayed cron jobs also resumed at that moment.
- The service was not OOM-killed and did not restart; this was an alive-but-unresponsive gateway failure.

## Affected Components

- Tools: terminal
- Gateway: Telegram and Discord liveness

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Linux x86_64
- Hermes: v0.18.2 (`2026.7.7.2`), installed commit `4281151ae859241351ba14d8c7682dc67ff4c126`
- Python used by Hermes: 3.11.15
- Backend: local terminal
- Gateway service limits: `MemoryHigh=2.4G`, `MemoryMax=3.0G`, 2 GiB swap available

The current upstream `main` at `c084085a3e520178fb3aa27c6ba7a411df8c79a0` still has the same unbounded capture/post-processing order.

## Debug Report

Not uploaded because this was a production gateway containing private messaging/configuration context. The evidence above is narrowly sanitized. I can provide additional sanitized diagnostics if needed.

## Root Cause Analysis

Current upstream behavior:

1. `tools/environments/base.py::_wait_for_process()` appends every decoded chunk to an unbounded `output_chunks` list.
2. Timeout and natural-exit paths call `"".join(output_chunks)`, creating another full-size string.
3. `tools/terminal_tool.py` passes the full string through sudo handling/detection and `transform_terminal_output` plugin hooks.
4. Only afterward does it read `get_max_bytes()` and truncate the result.

The configured 50 KB cap therefore limits only the final tool payload, not memory consumed while executing or processing the command.

## Proposed Fix

- Replace unbounded `output_chunks` retention with a bounded streaming collector that maintains the configured head/tail budget and an omitted-byte count.
- If full output is required for an opt-in plugin, spool it to a bounded/temporary file rather than the gateway heap.
- Apply sudo-failure checks and other scanners to bounded windows sufficient for their signatures.
- Add tests asserting that a very large producer returns bounded output while collector memory remains O(`max_bytes`).
- Add a continuous-output pipeline regression test verifying that foreground timeout kills the process group on schedule.
- Consider a gateway liveness watchdog or stronger isolation so terminal output processing cannot starve Discord heartbeats and Telegram polling.

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

With `compression.enabled: false`, hitting a context overflow produces a terminal error that explicitly tells the user to compact manually:

> ❌ Context overflow, but auto-compaction is disabled (compression.enabled: false).
> 💡 Run /compress to compact manually, /new to start fresh, switch to a larger-context model, or reduce attachments.

But following that advice fails on two surfaces:

- **Classic CLI** — `/compress` refuses: `(._.) Compression is disabled in config.` (`cli.py`, `_manual_compress`)
- **ACP adapter** — `/compact` refuses: `Context compression is disabled for this agent.` (`acp_adapter/server.py`, `_cmd_compact`)

The **gateway** `/compress` handler has no such gate, and the overflow path's own comment states the config flag governs *automatic* compaction only ("Forced compaction via `/compress` (`force=True`) is unaffected — it never reaches this loop"). So a user at a full window with compression off has no manual escape hatch on exactly the surfaces where the error directs them to use one.

## Reproduce

1. `compression.enabled: false` in config.yaml, small-context local model.
2. Converse until the provider returns a context-overflow error → terminal error message above.
3. Run `/compress` in the classic CLI → refused.

## Context

The CLI gate dates to the original `/compress` commit (30efc263f) and predates the overflow-path design. Fix proposed in PR #63630 (removes the stale gates, unifies `force=True` across manual-compaction call sites on CLI/ACP/TUI, gateway untouched).

items.title: # Bug: HTTP 429 error record persists in session context and cannot be cleared

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Describe the bug

When Hermes receives an HTTP 429 (rate limit) from an upstream provider during a conversation, the error message "API call failed after 3 retries: HTTP 429" gets permanently stuck in the session context. Even after switching to a different working provider, this error message reappears on every subsequent user turn within the same session. The only way to clear it is /reset or restarting Hermes entirely.

## To Reproduce

1. Use a rate-limited third-party provider (e.g., a proxy that returns 429)
2. Send a message → Hermes shows "API call failed after 3 retries: HTTP 429"
3. Switch to a working provider (official DeepSeek, Claude, etc.)
4. Send another message in the same session
5. The 429 error reappears again and again

## Expected behavior

- Error messages from old failed API calls should not pollute subsequent turns
- Session should recover automatically when user switches to a working provider
- Or there should be a command to clear only the error records without resetting the whole session

## Workaround

Only /reset or restarting Hermes clears it, but this loses the conversation flow.

## Environment

- Hermes: v0.18.2
- macOS 15.5
- Interface: Desktop App / WeChat bot
